The original Apple TV 4K launched in 2017 has just been added to Apple's list of "vintage" products. What does that actually mean?

Original Apple TV 4K labelled "vintage," repair service may be reduced

If you're still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K that launched nearly a decade ago, getting it repaired may soon become more complicated.

According to MacRumors, the original Apple TV 4K has been marked by Apple as a "vintage" product.

Apple maintains a list of vintage and obsolete products on its website.

  • "Vintage" means more than five years have passed since the product was discontinued
  • "Obsolete" means more than seven years have passed since the product was discontinued

If your product is marked as "obsolete," Apple will no longer provide service or hardware repairs.

If it's classified as "vintage," Apple will generally still offer repair service, but whether repairs can actually be carried out depends on parts availability.

So if you still have an original Apple TV 4K and think you might need a repair, get it sorted as soon as possible. Alternatively, you can keep an eye out for the next-generation Apple TV 4K expected to be announced at Tuesday's "Welcome home" event.

Still using the first-generation Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments section.
